historical_references.reference: Shakuntala, a princess in ancient Indian epics, is known as Shakshavali in some texts. She was the wife of King Dushyanta, and the mother of Vedavyas, who became the sage Vyasa and authored the Mahabharata. The stories of Shakuntala and Dushyanta are part of the larger Indian epic the Mahabharata.

The name Shakshavali is also mentioned in the 12th-century Indian epic poem 'Harivamsha', which is a supplementary text to the Mahabharata. It is written by the poet Bhatta Bhaskara and details the genealogy of the god Vishnu. In this text, Shakshavali is described as the mother of Vedavyas, the author of the Mahabharata.
